input_signals.name: CashEbitdaYieldBSAccrual
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: An operating-earnings yield built from EBITDA net of the balance-sheet working-capital accrual is a cleaner measure of distributable cash cheapness than any accounting-earnings yield.
input_signals.reasoning: Instead of ranking two separate channels, this embeds the Sloan-style balance-sheet accrual directly inside the numerator of the valuation ratio, so a firm looks cheap only if its operating profit is not financed by receivable/inventory build-ups. The balance-sheet accrual construction is independent of cash-flow-statement reporting conventions, giving a different measurement path than signals 1-3.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ebitda, sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) )

input_signals.name: SalesYieldReceivableBacked
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(recch, 0), COALESCE(invch, 0)), at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sales-based cheapness is trustworthy only when revenue is converted into cash rather than parked in receivables and inventory.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales-to-price avoids earnings management in the denominator of profitability but is vulnerable to channel-stuffing; recch and invch (cash-flow-statement decreases in receivables/inventory, positive when working capital releases cash) test exactly that conversion. COALESCE to zero is justified because an unreported working-capital line item means no disclosed change, not a missing firm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( add( coalesce( recch, 0 ), coalesce( invch, 0 ) ), at ) )

input_signals.name: ValueWithWorkingCapitalDiscipline
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms are rewarded when revenue is being generated with shrinking (not expanding) non-cash working capital, because a rising working-capital intensity of sales is the balance-sheet footprint of soft revenue recognition and predicts earnings reversal.
input_signals.reasoning: The valuation channel (book-to-market) and the accrual channel (change in non-cash working capital per dollar of sales) share no variable, so the composite genuinely combines two independent sources of information rather than re-deriving CFO/P from oancf twice. Scaling working capital by sales rather than assets makes the accrual leg a revenue-quality measure, distinguishing operationally lean cheap firms from cheap firms whose reported growth is trapped in receivables and inventory.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), neg( delta( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashEbitdaToEnterpriseValue
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-converted operating profit should be priced against the whole capital structure; the accrual-adjusted operating yield is informative about mispricing only once the leverage tilt in an equity-only deflator is removed.
input_signals.reasoning: This directly addresses the critic's objection to the gen-0 winner: an unlevered numerator over levered equity value created a leverage bet that plausibly contributed to the negative FF5 alpha, since leverage correlates with HML and CMA loadings. Keeping everything else identical makes the enterprise-value deflator a clean, single-design-choice test of whether the negative alpha was a leverage artifact.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ebitda, sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sub( add( dltt, dlc ), che ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapWithRisingDepreciationIntensity
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The long-lived-asset accrual channel works through depreciation adequacy: firms that let depreciation intensity drift down are stretching useful lives and capitalizing costs to prop up book earnings, so their cheapness is manufactured, whereas cheap firms with rising depreciation intensity are recognizing costs conservatively.
input_signals.reasoning: It resurrects the depreciation channel that scored highest with the critic but died at 0% coverage because industry operators are unavailable in this environment; using a within-firm 5-year trend instead of IND_RANK removes the capital-intensity confound through the firm's own history rather than through peers. This is the only proposal that sources accrual quality outside working capital, so it diversifies the archive's dominant channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( rank( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningsYieldWithStableAccruals
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings yield is informative only when the accrual process is stable; erratic year-to-year swings in non-cash working capital intensity indicate estimate-driven, non-persistent earnings, so apparent cheapness on those earnings is unreliable.
input_signals.reasoning: This restores the second-moment idea that the validator rejected earlier for lacking an accruals-exclusive variable, now built from act/lct so it qualifies and is measured on the balance sheet. It is the only proposal keyed to accrual *instability* rather than accrual level or slope, and it pairs with an earnings-yield rather than book-based valuation weight, so it teaches a different lesson than Signals 1-3.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( rank( neg( vol( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WeakestLinkCheapAndClean
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness and accounting quality are complements with no substitutability: a firm must clear both hurdles to be a genuine bargain, and failing either one is sufficient to disqualify it, so the binding constraint — the weaker of the two percentile scores — should price the stock.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN operator encodes a conjunctive (Leontief) interaction that is neither a rank sum, a rank product, nor a gate, so the long leg is cheap-and-clean while the short leg contains firms that fail on either dimension — a structurally different portfolio composition from every archive signal. Testing it tells us whether the value-trap mechanism is better described as a joint hurdle than as a continuous weighting, using the accrual channel that has already shown portfolio-level promise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapTwoChannelAccrualState
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Working-capital discipline and depreciation adequacy are two largely independent dimensions of accounting quality, so a cheap firm that scores well on both has genuinely cash-validated cheapness and the combined quality state should predict returns more reliably than either channel alone.
input_signals.reasoning: Both ingredient channels delivered positive but individually imprecise FF5 alphas (t = 2.70 and 1.46) from different parts of the accounting system — current operating assets versus long-lived assets — so averaging their ranks should cancel channel-specific noise and raise both fmb_tstat and ls_talpha rather than just relabel one of them. This is the batch's consolidation move, using the archive as evidence about which channels to combine.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapWithTaxVerifiedEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Income taxes payable are a third-party-verified claim that arises only when profits are real in the tax authority's eyes, so a cheap firm that persistently carries meaningful accrued taxes has earnings validated outside the accounting discretion of management, while a cheap firm reporting book profits with negligible tax liabilities is likely reporting accrual-inflated income.
input_signals.reasoning: This opens the tax channel, which is untouched in the archive and is economically independent of both working-capital slopes and depreciation adequacy — book-tax divergence is the classic external check on earnings quality. The three-year average implements the archive's clearest lesson (multi-year states beat one-year flows) while txp is a densely populated balance-sheet item, so coverage should match the study's norm rather than shrink like the cash-flow-statement lines.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( rank( ma( ratio( txp, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: HardAssetBookToMarket
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book equity is a mixture of hard components (cash, long-lived assets) and soft, estimate-laden net working capital (receivables and inventories net of operating liabilities); cheapness backed by hard book value is real, while cheapness backed mostly by soft working capital is an accounting artifact that reverses.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike a three-year accrual haircut, non-cash working capital is typically a large fraction of book equity — often tens of percent, and negative for cash-rich firms — so this construct reorders the value cross-section substantially rather than replicating HML's ranking. It gives the study one non-conditional test whose economic content is the *composition* of book value rather than its level, which is the mechanism by which HML mistakes soft-asset firms for bargains.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ceq, sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) )

input_signals.name: ThreeChannelQualityCheap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accounting quality supporting cheapness has three separable dimensions — working-capital discipline, depreciation adequacy, and the completed unwinding of past accrual bloat — and a cheap firm scoring well on all three has earnings that are simultaneously cash-converted, conservatively costed, and free of an unreversed overhang.
input_signals.reasoning: Two-channel averaging raised the FF5 alpha from 2.2% to 3.0% and the t-stat from 2.70 to 3.42, so the natural test is whether the third channel that also produced standalone positive alpha (accrual unwind, +1.6%, t 1.85) adds further independent information or is redundant with the working-capital slope. The three legs use different accounting objects (level slope, long-lived-asset charge, distance from own historical peak), so their errors should be weakly correlated.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), sumrank( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ), sub( ts_max( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ), 5 ), ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: QualityCompositeWithTaxCheck
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: External verification by the tax authority is a distinct form of earnings validation from internal cash conversion, so adding persistent accrued taxes to the quality composite should identify cheap firms whose profits are real to both the cash cycle and the taxman.
input_signals.reasoning: The tax channel standing alone had the highest Fama-MacBeth t-stat of any quality leg tested (2.57) but a weak alpha (+0.6%), the mirror image of the working-capital trend's profile, so combining them targets the study's exact weakness — jointly strong cross-sectional and portfolio evidence. Paired with Signal 1 it identifies which third channel carries incremental information rather than just averaging noise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), sumrank( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ), ma( ratio( txp, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BroadValueAmplifiedQuality
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book-to-market is a noisy proxy for cheapness — it misprices asset-light and write-down-scarred firms — so a two-measure value composite (book and sales relative to price) should identify the firms where accounting quality matters more accurately than book-to-market alone.
input_signals.reasoning: The amplifier determines *where* the accrual interaction is switched on, and the archive shows it materially changes results (yield-based amplifiers turned the alpha negative, the hard gate destabilized the portfolio), so improving its measurement is a substantive change rather than a relabeling. Sales-to-price is available for firms with distorted book equity, which should also stabilize the extreme buckets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sumrank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OwnHistoryCheapWithQuality
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Mispricing is best identified relative to a firm's *own* valuation history rather than the cross-section: a firm trading at the cheap end of its five-year book-to-market range while its accounting quality is improving has suffered a price decline unmatched by fundamentals.
input_signals.reasoning: A time-series cheapness amplifier is structurally orthogonal to HML — it contains no permanent industry or business-model value tilt, only firm-level valuation deviation — so it should isolate the accrual-quality interaction with even less factor contamination than cross-sectional B/M. This is the first valuation channel in the study measured in the time-series dimension, and it directly tests whether the interaction is about being cheap or about having become cheap.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OwnHistoryCheapThreeChannel
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm trading cheap relative to its own valuation history is a genuine bargain only when its accounting is validated on three fronts — working-capital discipline, depreciation adequacy and taxes actually accrued — and the tax channel supplies the cross-sectional information the balance-sheet slopes lack.
input_signals.reasoning: The two best gen-4 findings were independent of each other — the time-series amplifier improved the portfolio evidence (alpha 3.9%, t 4.12) while the tax leg improved the cross-sectional evidence (fmb 3.87) — and no signal has yet combined them, so this directly targets the stated objective of joint strength rather than one metric. All three quality channels use densely populated annual items, so coverage should hold near the study norm of 0.10.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), sumrank( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ), ma( ratio( txp, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OwnHistoryCheapNoAssetBloat
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual accumulation is not confined to working capital: a multi-year build-up of *total* net operating assets per dollar of sales — capitalized costs, acquired intangibles and unproductive plant as well as receivables and inventory — measures the full stock of unreversed accruals that will eventually be written down, so a dislocated-cheap firm shedding operating assets relative to sales is the credible bargain.
input_signals.reasoning: Every quality channel tested so far lives inside current assets and liabilities or in depreciation alone; net operating assets relative to sales spans both and captures capitalization decisions that working-capital measures miss entirely, making it the broadest untested accrual state in the resource menu. Pairing it with the study's best amplifier gives the new channel a fair test against the archive's incumbent.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), zscore( rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( sub( at, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SalesAnchoredOwnHistoryCheapQuality
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The valuation anchor used to identify dislocation should itself be free of accounting discretion: revenue is far harder to manipulate than book equity, so a firm priced cheaply against its own history of sales-to-price is dislocated for market reasons, and conditioning that dislocation on accrual quality isolates genuine mispricing.
input_signals.reasoning: Every amplifier tested so far uses book equity, which is contaminated by exactly the accrual and impairment decisions the quality leg is meant to police — a circularity that weakens the interaction, since write-downs mechanically move book-to-market. Replacing it with an own-history sales-to-price percentile keeps the time-series construction that carried all the portfolio evidence (alpha 3.9%, t 4.12) while removing accounting contamination from the valuation side, and unlike a cross-sectional sales yield it carries no permanent value tilt for HML to absorb.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OwnHistoryCheapSalesOutpacingAssets
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1)), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The classic fundamental-analysis red flag is operating current assets growing faster than revenue: receivables and inventory outrunning sales means demand is being met with credit terms and unsold stock, so a dislocated-cheap firm whose sales growth persistently exceeds its operating-asset growth has real, collectible revenue.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the price-driven "freshly cheap" amplifier — which was really a disguised reversal bet — with a new *quality* channel measured as a growth differential rather than a deflated level or slope, the Lev-Thiagarajan diagnostic that the archive has never tested. Using non-cash current assets (act − che), a strictly positive quantity, keeps GROWTH well behaved, and the three-year average suppresses the single-year noise that killed every one-year accrual channel in the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), zscore( rank( ma( sub( growth( sale, 1 ), growth( sub( act, che ), 1 ) ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OwnHistoryCheapRisingCashMargin
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness is validated not only by the absence of accrual build but by an improving *cash* margin after the depreciation charge that proxies the capital the business consumes; a dislocated-cheap firm whose post-depreciation cash margin has trended up for five years is earning more real cash per dollar of revenue than its price implies.
input_signals.reasoning: Every quality channel tested so far measures the *stock or slope of accruals* on the balance sheet; none measures accrual-free profitability dynamics, which is the economically prior question of whether the business is actually generating more cash per unit of sales. Subtracting depreciation from operating cash flow charges the firm for capital consumption, so the measure cannot be gamed by cutting maintenance capex the way a raw cash-margin trend can.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), zscore( rank( trend( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BothAnchorsCheapWithQuality
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A price dislocation is credible only when the firm is cheap versus its own history on both an accounting anchor (book) and a real-activity anchor (sales); if only one anchor is depressed, the "cheapness" is an artifact of a write-down or a margin collapse rather than of price.
input_signals.reasoning: The previous version averaged the two anchors, which contradicted its own conjunctive claim; taking the minimum of the two own-history percentiles implements the hypothesis literally, so a firm whose book-to-market is at a five-year high only because equity was written down scores low. Both legs are densely populated and purely time-series, keeping the amplifier free of the cross-sectional value tilt that has repeatedly produced negative FF5 alphas here.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ) ), zscore( sumrank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ), trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: NoRedFlagQualityOwnHistoryCheap
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The two accounting-quality dimensions that carry the archive's abnormal returns — working-capital discipline and depreciation adequacy — are complements rather than substitutes, so a cheap firm must clear both hurdles and a failure on either should not be offset by strength on the other.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier conjunctive attempt died at 0% coverage because it took MIN across the sparsely reported txp leg, so this version conjoins the two densely populated channels that jointly produced the best alpha in the study when averaged (+3.9%, t 4.12), making the additive-versus-conjunctive comparison a clean, interpretable contrast on identical inputs. It differs from WeakestLinkCheapAndClean, which took MIN *across* valuation and quality and thereby inherited the cross-sectional value tilt that drove that signal's alpha negative.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), min( zscore( rank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ) ) ), zscore( rank( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SelfFundedCleanCheapHurdles
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual-inflated earnings have to be financed: a firm whose reported cash conversion and depreciation look adequate but whose debt keeps rising relative to assets is not actually self-funding its operations, so financing self-sufficiency is a third, non-redundant hurdle a cheap firm must clear.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the rejected net-operating-asset hurdle, which was arithmetically nested inside the working-capital leg it was meant to police, the financing leg comes from the right-hand side of the balance sheet and can veto a different set of firms — those whose operating metrics look clean precisely because creditors are funding the gap. This makes the conjunction span the cash cycle, cost recognition and funding, the three ways a value trap can sustain the appearance of quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), min( min( zscore( rank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ) ) ), zscore( rank( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) ), zscore( rank( neg( trend( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 5 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: HardBookDislocationCleanCheap
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The valuation anchor should be purged of soft assets before dislocation is measured: cheapness relative to a firm's own history of *hard* book value — equity excluding net non-cash working capital — cannot be manufactured by receivable and inventory accumulation, so it identifies price dislocation rather than accounting inflation.
input_signals.reasoning: Hard book-to-market was tested only as a cross-sectional ratio, where it behaved like every other yield (fmb 2.29, alpha −1.3%), and the archive's central finding is that moving a valuation anchor from the cross-section into the firm's own time series flips those negative alphas positive (book anchor: −2.7% cross-sectionally versus +3.9% in TS form). This is therefore a substantive test of an accrual-purged anchor in the dimension that works, not a repetition of the tax-veto structure whose coverage failure is now diagnosed as NaN propagation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( sub( ceq, sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ), min( zscore( rank( neg( trend( ratio( wcap, sale ), 5 ) ) ) ), zscore( rank( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: HardBookWithStableAccrualProcess
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Direction and stability of the accrual process are separate credibility dimensions: a dislocated-cheap firm whose working capital is both trending down and varying little year to year has a predictable, estimate-light accounting process, whereas an erratic accrual process signals discretionary management regardless of its trend.
input_signals.reasoning: Accrual volatility was tested once, under an earnings-yield amplifier that we now know contaminates any spread with HML exposure (alpha −1.7%), so the second-moment dimension has never had a fair test in the architecture that works. Pairing it additively with the trend under the purified anchor keeps coverage dense and asks whether stability adds information beyond direction — the one moment of the accrual distribution still unresolved.

input_signals.hypothesis: External tax verification and internal cash conversion are the two independent credibility checks, and giving the tax check equal weight alongside working-capital discipline — under an anchor that cannot be inflated by accruals — should deliver cross-sectional and portfolio evidence simultaneously.
input_signals.reasoning: The tax channel has repeatedly moved the Fama-MacBeth slope (2.57 standalone; 3.87 inside a composite) but never received more than quarter weight in a composite that also had a strong anchor, and its only conjunctive test failed on NaN propagation, so equal additive weight with a dense partner leg is the untested configuration. Using the hard-book anchor addresses the archive's other regularity — that alpha lives in the purified own-history anchors — so this is aimed squarely at joint strength rather than at one metric.

input_signals.name: StandardizedDislocationCleanCheap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MA(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), VOL(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is the *size* of the valuation dislocation relative to the firm's own normal variation: a book-to-market two standard deviations above its own five-year mean is a far stronger mispricing candidate than one merely at the top of a five-point rank, and stable-valuation firms need smaller absolute moves to be dislocated than volatile ones.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic has twice noted that a five-observation TS_RANK is coarse and lumpy, and this replaces it with a firm-specific standardized deviation that preserves magnitude and scales by the firm's own valuation volatility — a new economic claim (dislocation should be measured in units of the firm's own risk) rather than an operator swap between two archive signals. The outer cross-sectional RANK keeps the amplifier a strictly positive weight so the quality leg's sign is never flipped for expensive firms, which was the design feature that made the multiplicative architecture HML-neutral.

input_signals.name: InvestedCapitalDislocationQuality
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The dislocation that accounting quality should be conditioned on belongs to the *business*, not to the levered equity stub: comparing book invested capital (equity plus net debt) with the market value of that same invested capital measures how cheaply the whole enterprise trades relative to its own history, free of leverage amplification.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic correctly identified a numerator/denominator mismatch in the previous version — book equity over enterprise value mechanically penalizes levered firms — so this puts net invested capital in both numerator and denominator, which is the coherent capital-level analogue of book-to-market. Since leverage is the last known contaminant of the own-history anchor after the soft-asset purification worked (fmb 3.10, Sharpe 0.45), this tests whether de-levering the dislocation measure further sharpens the interaction while keeping dense balance-sheet coverage.

input_signals.name: HardBookChronicAccrualLevel
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Direction of working-capital intensity and the chronic *magnitude* of annual accruals are different facts: a firm can be tightening its ratio while still booking large accruals every year, so a dislocated-cheap firm is credible only when its average annual accrual per dollar of sales is small as well as falling.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the payout channel — which the critic rightly judged a payer dummy and weak evidence about earnings, since distributions can be debt-financed — with the accrual flow itself, averaged over five years so it measures habitual reliance rather than the single-year change that failed early in the archive. Both legs come from densely reported balance-sheet items under the purified hard-book anchor, so coverage should hold near 0.10 where the study's evidence has been reliable.

input_signals.name: CapitalDislocationLevelAndTrend
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Credible cheapness requires accruals that are both small in habitual magnitude and falling in intensity; the chronic five-year average accrual per dollar of sales and the direction of working-capital intensity are separate facts, and neither the depreciation leg nor the trend alone captures the former.
input_signals.reasoning: The chronic-level channel produced alpha +3.2% (t 2.74, Sharpe 0.36) when paired with the hard-book anchor, and it avoids the asset-growth confound that the critic repeatedly flagged in the depreciation-intensity leg, so pairing it with the strongest anchor tests a quality composite that is entirely working-capital-based but spans magnitude and direction. It is the most economically pure statement of the value-trap mechanism the study has assembled.

input_signals.name: CapitalDislocationAccrualShareOfProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), ADD(ABS(ib), dp)), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The value-trap story is literally about the *share of reported profit that is accrual rather than cash*, so the right quality measure deflates accruals by the firm's earnings capacity rather than by sales or assets: a dislocated-cheap firm whose accruals consume a small fraction of its profit is reporting cash-backed income.
input_signals.reasoning: Every accrual leg in this study has been deflated by sales or assets, which measures accrual intensity of *activity*; deflating by earnings capacity measures accrual intensity of *reported profit*, which is the quantity the hypothesis is actually about and which reorders firms with high accruals but very high profits differently from firms with modest accruals and no profits. Using ABS(ib) plus depreciation in the denominator keeps the ratio finite for loss-makers and near-zero-earnings firms, the failure mode that makes naive accrual-to-earnings ratios explode.

input_signals.name: OneSidedAccrualPenaltyCheap
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(MAX(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5), SUB(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5), TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The mechanism is one-sided: building working capital destroys the credibility of cheap earnings, but shrinking it faster and faster adds no further information once the firm is already releasing capital, so the penalty should apply only to the positive part of the accrual trend.
input_signals.reasoning: Every quality leg tested so far is linear in the accrual state, which implicitly assumes ever-greater working-capital contraction is ever-better news — economically doubtful, since aggressive liquidation is a distress symptom, not a quality signal. Truncating the trend at zero is a genuine functional-form claim about the mechanism rather than a new input, and pairing it with the depreciation leg inside SUMRANK breaks the tie mass created among all firms whose working capital is already falling.

input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness should compare the book value of the *operating* capital a firm employs — assets excluding cash, net of non-debt operating liabilities — with the market value of exactly that operating capital, so the anchor measures how cheaply the market prices the productive asset base whose accounting quality the second leg audits.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic correctly showed the previous version's numerator collapsed to non-current assets while its denominator priced all operating assets, a base mismatch; defining the numerator as net operating assets and the denominator as enterprise value net of cash puts both sides on the same operating-capital base. This makes the anchor the direct book-to-market of the operating business, which is the object the accrual channels measure, rather than a mixture of equity, cash and leverage effects.
